rationale: B wins because it found the accountability story A left on the floor: "Perplexity now earns a fee when you buy what it recommends" turns the shopping launch into a conflict-of-interest question, not just commerce plumbing. A is clean, but "One AI app, two new ways to take a cut" is mostly a competent bundle of the first two angles, not a fresh newsroom doorway. B has a few overclaims, but its best angle gives a tougher editor more to work with.
gaps_in_A: A misses the user-trust angle. "Perplexity turns its answer engine into a checkout" frames the launch as a commerce-channel story, but never asks whether referral fees change rankings, labeling, or recommendation integrity.
"One AI app, two new ways to take a cut" is useful synthesis, but it is close to repackaging the publisher and shopping facts instead of adding a new protagonist.

"What Perplexity's multi-billion valuation says about the AI bubble" is rightly refused as too broad, but A throws away the narrower valuation question the update does support: whether these revenue lines can justify a multi-billion private valuation.
"hallucinated_fact" is the wrong tag for the refused query-volume angle. The query count is in the update; the unsupported leap is "search powerhouse."
gaps_in_B: "This is the company's first structural answer to that fight" adds "first" without support. The update says the program launches now, not that Perplexity has never offered another answer before.
"takes a referral fee on every sale" overstates the mechanics. The update says Perplexity earns a referral fee; it does not prove every in-app purchase carries one.
"The launch is the first concrete monetization signal since the raise" invents business history. The update gives a recent valuation, not a clean before-and-after monetization narrative.
"Investors and rivals will read it as the thesis" is pundit air unless B can attach an investor, competitor reaction, or prior financing narrative.
